english_abstract: This paper investigates grant-free random access in low Earth orbit satellite Internet-of-Things systems without global navigation satellite system (GNSS) assistance. We firstly propose a multi-frame transmission scheme with affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) to handle the large differential delay and Doppler shift at the satellite receiver, and derive the input-output relationship. Subsequently, we learn a score-based generative channel prior directly on the AFDM effective channel with fractional delay and Doppler, without restrictive sparse or grid-aligned channel assumptions. The training uses colored Gaussian noise to account for correlations in the denoiser input error. The learned prior is then incorporated into a message passing (MP) receiver as a minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoiser, providing posterior mean and variance estimates without calculating high-dimensional integrals. To incorporate activity uncertainty into channel estimation, a learned density ratio estimator uses the denoiser input and output to estimate activity probabilities, enabling joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE). Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed receiver outperforms the baseline receiver in terms of activity detection and channel estimation.
